extraction.Name: Charlotte Huebner
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent to her allotment for the reason that she knew she could not pay the taxes, but that she was told that if she did not take the patent and pay the taxes that she would lose the land and she was advised to take it by the Farmer of her district as well as by the people in the Agency Office, so she did
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged it and bought a bunch of cattle, thinking that she could make money enough out of them to pay the taxes and pay for the cattle and clear the land, but the price of cattle went down so she lost the cattle and the land too
extraction.Buyer: Land and cattle were mortgaged to Harry Wentzy, Rapid City, So. Dak. and he foreclosed the mortgage and took the land and cattle both
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: could not pay the taxes, so she mortgaged it
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent but in exceedingly poor health, having been laid up all last summer, suffering from kidney and heart trouble and has fainting spells; has a husband that is not at all well and six children depending on her for support; cattle cost $5100.00 and were included in the mortgage along with the land; document number No. 03037; subscribed and sworn before notary public on the 5th day of November, 1928, in County of Shannon, State of South Dakota | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 48 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal. | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County (South Dakota)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
Pine Ridge tribe field had 40+ string variants across the corpus. Consolidating to canonical 'Pine Ridge' for clean tabulation while preserving original variant in NOTES for audit.
